Wall Street wanted rate cuts. The Fed just signalled the opposite.

Minutes from the October meeting show almost all Fed officials expect to RAISE rates, not lower them. They held at 3.75–4% in a 10–2 vote, with two members pushing for an immediate hike. Their preferred inflation gauge is running at 3.6% — nearly double the 2% target — and the minutes name the AI build-out as one more thing pushing prices up.

Higher rates flow straight to your mortgage, car loan and credit card. Savers win, borrowers pay.

My take: if you've been waiting for cheap money to come back, the Fed is telling you not to count on it yet.

Are you planning around higher rates — or still betting on cuts in 2027? 👇
